*reasoning in the farmer's voice:*

Fifty years I've been on this land. Me and the old lady, 24 mu between us. Always split it half wheat, half maize — that's how everyone does it here, and the ground likes the rotation. We're too old now for heavy work, so the combine and the planter, I hire. Pay some, but my back won't do it anymore.

**Wheat (12 mu).** Plant mid-October, after the autumn rains settle the dust. I put down one bag of compound — the 15-15-15 — per mu before plowing, fifty kilos, that's what I always do. Come spring at jointing, if the wheat looks pale I topdress urea, about fifteen kilos a mu. Water three times: once before the freeze so the roots don't dry, once at jointing, once when the grain is filling. My neighbor Old Wang says the grain-filling water matters most, and I agree — that's where the weight comes from. Combine comes early June. Usually get around 450 kg/mu if the spring isn't too dry.

**Maize (12 mu).** Goes in right after wheat, no more than three-four days' gap — no time to sit around. The no-till planter drops seed and a bit of fertilizer together, forty kilos compound per mu. When it's knee-high to waist-high I put urea down between the rows, fifteen kilos a mu. Summer rain usually takes care of the rest, but if July turns dry I'll run the well once. Spray herbicide early for weeds. Sometimes corn borer shows, then I spray. Harvest end of September. Five hundred kilos a mu is normal.

Seeds I buy in town — whatever the agri shop has that everyone's using. Don't save my own, the hybrid maize doesn't work that way anyway. Total cash out maybe ten thousand yuan, give or take. Not much room for mistakes at this age.
